short: Taehyoung Kim is a research engineer at Fraunhofer IVI working on robotic perception and aerial autonomy. His research spans video understanding, multimodal sensing, and semantic 3D mapping, with a focus on connecting research ideas to working robotic systems.

journey.title: Associate Researcher
journey.text: I work on aerial autonomy, connecting data and perception research with deployed robotic systems. My work includes temporally consistent video segmentation (SSP, CVPR 2025), efficient dataset annotation, and training and deploying models on onboard hardware. I’m also developing language-driven mission planning that connects vision-language models with robotic software.

journey.title: Research Internship
journey.text: I worked on learning-based UAV path planning, exploring how supervised and reinforcement learning could help an aerial robot plan its route. This work formed my aerospace master’s thesis, “From Supervised to Reinforced: A One-Shot Deep Learning Approach to UAV Path Planning.”

journey.title: M.Sc. Aerospace Engineering
journey.text: I focused my master’s thesis on learning-based UAV path planning, bringing together my interests in flight, machine learning, and autonomous decision-making.

journey.title: Working Student
journey.text: I worked part-time at Azena in Munich alongside my studies.

journey.title: Research Internship
journey.text: I worked on multi-physical modeling of quadrotor energy dynamics and reinforcement learning for damaged micro aerial vehicles, including fault-tolerant quadrotor control.

journey.title: M.Sc. Power Engineering
journey.text: My thesis, “Fault-Tolerant Quadrotor Controller Design Using Deep Reinforcement Learning,” explored how a controller could learn to keep a damaged quadrotor flying.

journey.title: B.Sc. Mechanical Engineering
journey.text: I studied mechanical engineering at Pusan National University.
